magnetic confinement: The tokamak uses a combination of toroidal and poloidal magnetic fields to confine the plasma.

Inside the tokamak, magnetic coils keep the plasma away from the walls of the vessel.
other fusion and nuclear: The Sun produces energy by fusing hydrogen into helium in its core.
A fission reactor uses a combination of uranium fuel rods and control rods.
In inertial confinement fusion, powerful lasers compress a small pellet of fuel.
other electromagnetism: The electric motor uses a combination of magnets and coils to produce rotation.
An MRI scanner uses a strong magnetic field to create an image of the body.
A transformer employs two coils wound around an iron core.
